case_name: Dataram Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh

pages.text:
REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 227 OF 2018

DATARAM SINGH ... APPELLANT
VERSUS
STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH & ANR. ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

DEEPAK GUPTA, J.

1. A fundamental postulate of criminal jurisprudence is the presumption of innocence, meaning thereby that a person is believed to be innocent until found guilty. Freedom of an individual is of utmost importance in our constitutional governance, enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

2. It is a well-settled principle of criminal law that bail is the rule and committal to jail is an exception. The grant of bail is an exercise of judicial discretion under Section 437 and Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC). The discretion must be exercised judiciously and not arbitrarily or mechanically.

3. The conditions for grant of bail must not be onerous or unreasonable so as to render the grant illusory. The court must examine whether the accused is likely to flee from justice, tamper with evidence, or influence witnesses.
